When Allah decrees in heaven the angels beat their wings in submission, while devils eavesdrop in a chain, passing words to fortune-tellers who add a hundred lies.
From Safa the Prophet warns Quraysh of a terrible punishment; Abu Lahab curses him, and the verse on Abu Lahab is revealed.
The Prophet tells Abu Dharr the sun goes and prostrates beneath Allah's Throne, the meaning of verse 36.38 on the sun running its fixed course.
The Prophet says no one has the right to be better than Jonah bin Matta, and whoever says the Prophet is better than him lies.
Ibn Abbas prostrates in Surat Sad because the Prophet was told to follow the guidance of prophets such as David, who prostrated.
A jinn demon tried to disturb the Prophet's prayer; he overpowered it and meant to tie it to a pillar, but released it recalling Solomon's prayer for a unique kingdom.
Ibn Mas'ud explains the Smoke as the haze starving Quraysh saw in the famine the Prophet invoked; the punishment lifted, they reverted, and Allah destroyed them at Badr.
Pagans guilty of many murders and adulteries ask whether their past can be expiated, and verse 25.68 is revealed, with another telling them not to despair of Allah's mercy.
A rabbi says Allah will hold all creation on His fingers, and the Prophet smiles agreement; Allah will grasp the earth, roll up the heavens and say: I am King.
The Prophet will raise his head first after the second trumpet and see Moses hanging on the Throne; forty separate the two blasts, and bodies are rebuilt from the coccyx.
Asked the worst thing the pagans did to the Prophet, Abdullah bin Amr tells how Uqba throttled him at the Ka'bah until Abu Bakr pushed him away.
Men of Quraysh and Thaqif argue whether Allah hears their talk, loud or low, and the verse on their ears, eyes and skins testifying against them is revealed.
Ibn Abbas explains verse 42.23: every branch of Quraysh was related to the Prophet, who asked only that they be kind to him for that kinship.
The Prophet recites from the pulpit the verse in which the people of Hell cry to Malik to have his Lord make an end of them.
Ibn Mas'ud says the Smoke was the haze Quraysh saw in the famine the Prophet invoked; relief came, they reverted and were seized at Badr, and five events have passed.
Allah says the son of Adam hurts Him by abusing Time, though He is Time, all things are in His Hands, and He turns the night and day.
Marwan claims the verse on one who says 'Fie' to his parents was revealed about Abdur-Rahman bin Abu Bakr, and Aisha replies nothing was revealed about them but her innocence.
The Prophet only smiled, never laughing loudly, and showed concern at clouds and wind, fearing punishment, as some people were punished by a wind they took for rain.
When creation was done the womb sought refuge from those who sever ties, and Allah promised to favour whoever keeps them and withhold from whoever severs them.
Umar, unanswered three times while travelling at night, fears revelation about himself, but the Prophet recites the new surah on a manifest victory, which Anas says means Hudaybiyyah.
On the day of the Conquest of Mecca the Prophet recited Surat al-Fath in a vibrating, pleasant voice.
The Prophet prayed at night until his feet swelled and cracked, though forgiven his past and future faults, wishing to be a thankful slave; when old he prayed sitting.
Verse 48.8 appears in the Torah with more: the Prophet as Allah's slave named Al-Mutawakkil, not harsh or loud, forgiving, through whom a crooked nation is guided.
A companion's horse kept jumping while he recited the Quran, and the Prophet said it was tranquillity descending because of the recitation.
Jabir says they were one thousand four hundred on the day of Hudaybiyyah.
Abdullah bin Mughaffal, one of those at the tree, reports that the Prophet forbade throwing small stones with two fingers and urinating where one bathes.
At Siffin Sahl bin Hunaif recalls Hudaybiyyah, when Umar protested to the Prophet and Abu Bakr against returning without fighting, and Surat al-Fath was revealed.
Abu Bakr and Umar raise their voices arguing over a governor for Bani Tamim, and the verse against raising voices above the Prophet's comes; Thabit bin Qais is promised Paradise.
Hell keeps asking for more until Allah puts His Foot over it; Paradise and Hell argue over who enters them, and Allah says each will have its fill.
Looking at the full moon, the Prophet says believers will see their Lord as clearly, so they should not miss the prayers before sunrise and sunset.
Ibn Abbas says Allah ordered His Prophet to glorify Him after all prayers, the meaning of 'after the prayers' in the verse.
Being sick, Um Salama is told to perform Tawaf riding behind the people, while the Prophet prays beside the Ka'bah reciting 'By the Mount'.
Hearing the Prophet recite Surat at-Tur in the Maghrib prayer, Jubair's heart nearly flew at the verses asking whether they were created by nothing or are the creators.
Aisha says whoever claims Muhammad saw his Lord, knows tomorrow or concealed any revelation is a liar, citing verses, and that he saw Gabriel in his true form twice.
On verses 53.9-18, Ibn Mas'ud reports that the Prophet saw Gabriel with six hundred wings and saw a green screen covering the horizon.
Lat was a man who mixed sawiq for pilgrims; one who swears by Lat and Uzza must affirm Allah's oneness; reverence for Manat kept some from Safa and Marwa.
The Prophet prostrated on finishing Surat an-Najm and all with him prostrated, Muslims, pagans, jinn and humans, except Umaiya bin Khalaf, who prostrated on a handful of dust.
In the Prophet's lifetime the moon split into two parts when the people of Mecca asked for a sign, and he told them to witness it.
The Prophet recited 'Fahal min Muddakir' with a d, and corrected Abdullah when he recited it with dh.
At Badr the Prophet pleads for Allah's promise until Abu Bakr stops him, then recites that their multitude will flee; Aisha recalls 54.46 coming at Mecca in her childhood.
